blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.
blocks.zh: 目前由音频驱动的视频传播模型可以合成现实的谈话头视频,但一般需要数十个在多秒视频块上的传播解码步骤,使其不适于语音助理和虚拟异形等流媒体应用,因为低纬度和在线因果生成需要属性. AURA 以滚动 KV 缓存按块生成视频块, 只需要当前块的音频开始生成, 而不是像双向模型那样多秒的音频外观。 它有两种大小:AURA 1.3B流576p视频实时在单一的GPU上播放(20.7fps为16Hz回放速率),使其适合交互式的avatar应用,以及AURA 5B流720p视频在9.7fps. 我们的两阶段蒸馏管道首先使因果学生与老师对齐,通过培训使老师的轨迹与传播步骤较少,以及一个块形的滑动窗口因果关注罩相匹配,然后应用分布匹配抖动(DMD)与落后的模拟来缩小剩余的质量差距. 在标准谈话头基准上,AURA 1.3B运行速度比自己的双向教师快23x,并以较低的分辨率达到与TalkVerse相当的质量,AURA 5B与其TalkVerse老师在720p同时运行速度更快. 为了支持可复制性和对流体化的造型的进一步研究,我们释放了两种模型的重量,以及30K合成视频的数据集及其预算的教师轨迹.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Recent speech-to-speech models [ 12 , 41 ] are able to model full-duplex voice interaction
in real-time, paving the way for voice assistants that hold natural and smooth conversations. However, these models only generate audio signal.
In contrast, human spoken communication relies on visual cues and facial expressions, via an interplay of the audio and visual modalities. For instance,
lip motion alters perceived phonemes [ 36 ] , visual cues sharpen comprehension in noise [ 47 ] , and an embodied talking face enhances the sense of social presence over voice alone [ 6 ] .
To model such behaviors, audio-driven video generation models can synthesize talking-head videos from a reference image and an input speech audio, enabling applications such as virtual avatars, synthetic presenters, and non-player characters in games.
All these applications, however, share a common constraint: the avatar must be generated on-the-fly, as the audio arrives, from a stream of audio of unbounded duration.
blocks.zh:
近期的语音对语音模型[12,41]能够模拟全复式语音交互
在实时中,为语音助理进行自然和顺畅的对话铺平道路。 然而,这些模型只产生音频信号.
相比之下,人类的口语交流依赖于视觉提示和面部表情,通过音频和视觉模式的相互作用. 比如说,
嘴唇运动会改变感知的电话 [36],视觉提示会提高噪音中的理解 [47],而一个隐含的说话面孔会增强社会存在的意识,而不是单独的声音 [6].
为了模拟这种行为,音频驱动的视频生成模型可以从参考图像和输入语音音频合成说话头视频,使虚拟异形,合成演示人,游戏中非玩家角色等应用得以实现.
然而,所有这些应用程序都有一个共同的制约:在音频到达时,必须从无限制持续时间的音频流中在飞行中生成浮雕。

blocks.en:
State-of-the-art talking-head models such as TalkVerse [ 52 ] and Wan-S2V [ 17 ] produce high-quality audio-driven videos but are ill-suited to the streaming setting. Because they rely on bidirectional attention, they must generate entire video chunks of several seconds at once, running dozens of denoising steps over the full chunk before producing any frame, which on a single GPU takes minutes per chunk.
Recently, CausVid [ 59 ] and Self-Forcing [ 23 ] have explored distilling such bidirectional video diffusion teachers into few-step causal students that generate video chunk by chunk in an autoregressive manner. However, these methods target only the text-to-video and image-to-video settings. Extending this approach to the audio-driven setting, where the model must additionally track a dense time-aligned speech signal, has so far been demonstrated only on much larger models (14–18B parameters) [ 24 , 42 , 33 ] , which remain too large for real-time inference on a single GPU (only 2 fps). A second obstacle is the scarcity of suitable training data: existing public talking-head datasets such as Hallo3 [ 9 ] and CelebV [ 63 ] consist of clips too short to cover the chunk length of modern teachers like TalkVerse, ruling them out for distillation (see Section 3.6 ).
blocks.zh:
TalkVerse[52],Wan-S2V[17]等最先进的谈话头型,制作高质量的音频驱动视频,但不适合流媒体环境. 因为它们依赖于双向的注意,它们必须一次生成数秒的整段视频块,在产生任何帧之前在整块上运行数十个调音步骤,在单个GPU上每块需要几分钟的时间.
最近,CausVid [59] 和Self-Forcing [23] 探讨了如何将这种双向视频传播教师分解成几个步骤的因果学生,以自动递减的方式逐块生成视频。 然而,这些方法只针对文本到视频和图像到视频设置. 将这种方法扩展至音频驱动的设置,该模型必须额外跟踪一个密集的时间相通的语音信号,到目前为止,它只表现在更大的模型(14–18B参数)[24,42,33]上,这些模型仍然太大,无法对单个GPU进行实时推断(只有2英尺). 第二个障碍是缺乏适当的培训数据:现有的公共谈话头数据集,如Hallo3[9]和CelebV[63],由短片组成,无法覆盖TalkVerse等现代教师的块长度,排除了它们进行蒸馏(见第3.6节)。

blocks.en:
We introduce AURA, a family of causal few-step speech-to-video (S2V) models that generate streaming talking-head videos from live audio. In particular, AURA 1.3B runs in real time, generating 576 576 p video at 20.7 20.7 frames per second for a 16 16 Hz playback rate on a single GPU, which makes it directly usable for the interactive applications above, such as a talking face for a voice assistant. AURA 5B targets higher resolution: it streams 720 720 p video at 9.7 9.7 fps, a 17 × 17\times speedup over its TalkVerse teacher. For training, we generate and release a new talking-head dataset comprising 30 30 K videos ( 38.7 38.7 hours) produced with TalkVerse, conditioned on reference images and text descriptions from the Hallo3 dataset [ 9 ] and synthetic speech audio.
To train our model, we use a two-stage distillation pipeline, similar to CausVid:
Stage 1 first trains the causal student to match the bidirectional TalkVerse teacher’s Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) trajectories in order to reduce the gap between the bidirectional teacher and the causal student architecture.
Then, Stage 2 closes the few-step gap with Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) and backward simulation : by training the student on intermediate states from its own denoising rollouts, the Stage 2 loss reflects accumulating errors the student may actually produce at inference.
To further improve efficiency, we train the model to support chunk-wise causal sliding window attention, allowing us to use a rolling KV cache with bounded memory at inference. We also use a single KV cache for all diffusion denoising timesteps, further reducing memory footprint.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍AURA, 一个由几步语音到视频(S2V)模式组成的家族, 特别是AURA 1.3B实时运行,以每秒20.7个20.7帧的速度生成576 576个p视频,在单一的GPU上以16个16Hz的回放速率播放,这使得它可以直接用于上面的交互应用,比如语音助理的说话面. AURA 5B的目标是更高的分辨率:它以9.7 9.7 英尺的速度流出720 720p的视频,一个17×17\时的速度超过它的TalkVerse老师. 为了进行培训,我们制作并发布了一个新的对话头数据集,其中包括与TalkVerse公司制作的30 K视频(38.7 38.7小时),并以哈洛3数据集的参考图像和文本描述以及合成语音音频为条件。
为了训练我们的型号,我们使用两阶段蒸馏管道,类似于CausVid:
第1阶段首先训练因果学生,以匹配双向TalkVerse教师的普通差异方程(ODE),以减少双向教师与因果学生架构之间的差距.
然后,第2阶段缩小了与分配匹配消化(DMD)和后向模拟的几步差距:通过对学生进行中间状态的培训,使其从其自身的去诺启动,第2阶段的损失反映了学生在推论中实际可能产生的累积错误.
为了进一步提高效率,我们训练该模型以支持断点因果滑动窗口的注意,使我们能够使用一个滚动的 KV 缓存,在推论中带有内存。 我们还对所有扩散去诺定时步骤使用单一的KV缓存,进一步减少记忆足迹.

blocks.en: With this approach, on standard talking-avatar benchmarks, AURA 5B matches or improves on its bidirectional teacher on visual quality (FVD [ 50 ] and JEDi [ 34 ] metrics) and audio-visual alignment, while running 17 × 17\times faster with only four denoising steps per chunk, and AURA 1.3B reaches a comparable quality at a lower resolution and in real time ( 23 × 23\times faster than its own teacher). Both models are faster than all baselines we compare against in the same single-GPU setting. Figure 1 shows an excerpt of qualitative samples generated by both models, as well as their speed–quality tradeoff against prior work.
blocks.zh: 采用这种方法,在标准对话-avatar基准上,AURA 5B在视觉质量(FVD[50]和JEDI[34]度量衡)和视听对齐方面与双向教师相匹配或改进,同时运行17×17\次,每块只有4个除音步骤,AURA 1.3B在低分辨率和实时(23×23\次比自己的老师快)达到可比质量. 两种模型都比我们在同一个单GPU设置中比较的所有基线都快. 图1摘录了两个模型所产生的质量样本,以及它们与以前工作之间的速度和质量权衡。

blocks.en: In summary, we introduce AURA, which makes the following contributions: • A two-stage distillation method (ODE-trajectory initialization followed by Distribution Matching Distillation with backward simulation) paired with a streaming inference scheme based on a rolling KV cache of past chunks, shared by both models; • AURA 5B , a causal few-step S2V model that matches or improves on its bidirectional teacher on FVD and JEDi metrics, with a 17 × 17\times speedup. Our inference pipeline streams 720 720 p video at 9.7 9.7 fps on a single GPU, the highest throughput among audio-driven baselines we compare against; • AURA 1.3B , a smaller model trained with the same pipeline, which streams 576 576 p video in real time on a single GPU ( 20.7 20.7 fps generated for a 16 16 Hz playback rate), a 23 × 23\times speedup over its own bidirectional teacher; • A public dataset of 30 30 K talking-head videos generated by TalkVerse from synthetic speech, released both as decoded videos and as the latent ODE trajectories of the teacher, to support future research on streaming S2V distillation, together with the weights of our 1.3 1.3 B teacher and its own 30 30 K ODE trajectories; • A live demo coupling AURA 1.3B with Unmute, a cascaded voice assistant built on Kyutai’s streaming speech-to-text and text-to-speech models [ 60 ] and a text LLM, in which users hold a natural spoken conversation with a synthetic avatar in real time on a single H100 GPU, available at kyutai.org/aura .
blocks.zh: 简而言之,我们介绍了AURA,它做出了以下贡献: • 双阶段蒸馏法(ODE-trajective初始化,然后是向后模拟的分布配对),与基于过去块的滚动KV缓存的流推法方案配对,两个模型共享; • AURA 5B,一个因果的几步S2V模型,在FVD和JEdi度量上与双向老师匹配或改进,其速度为17×17\时. AURA 1.3B,是一个经过同一管道培训的较小的模型,它实时流出576 576 p 视频在一个单一的GPU上(为16赫兹回放速率生成20.7 20.7 ps),一个23×23\时速加速在自己的双向教师身上; 由TalkeVerse从合成演讲中生成的30 K谈话头视频组成的公共数据集,既作为解码视频发布,又作为教师潜伏的ODE导轨; 支持未来对流S2V蒸馏的研究,同时支持我们1.3 B教师的重量和我们自己的30 KODE导轨迹; 现场演示将AURA 1.3B与UMUTE连接起来,由Kyutai的流传语音对文本和文本对流模型[60] 和一个文本LLLM,用户用一个合成的GLM进行自然对话。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Image Generative models have evolved through several paradigms:
Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) [ 18 , 25 , 4 ] are efficient as they generate images in a single forward pass but suffer from known limitations around mode coverage and training stability. More recently, diffusion models [ 20 , 45 , 15 , 44 , 40 , 26 ] and flow matching [ 30 , 32 ] have become the dominant paradigm for image generation. Indeed, both frameworks are closely related and model data through an iterative multi-step refinement process, yielding stable training with high sample diversity but at the cost of slow sampling. Most modern large-scale video generators, including our teacher TalkVerse [ 52 ] , are trained under the flow matching framework, and our work also builds on this formulation.
blocks.zh:
图像基因模型通过几个范式演变而来:
General Aversarial Networks [GANs] [18, 25, 4]是高效的,因为它们在一个单一的前进通道中生成图像,但是在模式覆盖和培训稳定性方面受到已知的限制. 最近,传播模式[20,45,15,44,40,26]和流量匹配[30,32]已成为图像生成的主要范例. 事实上,这两个框架都通过迭代的多步骤完善过程,彼此密切相关,形成稳定的培训,具有高度的样本多样性,但以缓慢取样为代价。 大多数现代大型视频发电机,包括我们的教师TalkVerse[52],都是在流量匹配框架下培训的,我们的工作也以这一表述为基础。

blocks.en:
Video Diffusion Models. Recent work has further scaled diffusion for video generation. Early efforts such as Imagen Video [ 21 ] , Make-A-Video [ 43 ] , Align Your Latents [ 3 ] , and Stable Video Diffusion [ 2 ] extended image diffusion to short clips, typically by inflating 2D architectures with temporal layers. More recent open-source and industrial models, Sora [ 5 ] , Movie Gen [ 38 ] , Open-Sora [ 62 ] , CogVideoX [ 56 ] , HunyuanVideo [ 27 ] , and Wan [ 51 ] — adopt diffusion transformer (DiT) architectures and operate in a compressed latent space, scaling to 720 720 p– 1080 1080 p resolutions and minute-long clips. These models are typically non-causal: they generate the entire video sequence jointly over 50 50 or more denoising steps, and are thus not well adapted to the latency requirements of streaming applications. Current SotA talking-head models are based on such architectures. For instance, Hallo3 [ 9 ] adapts CogVideoX [ 56 ] for portrait animation with a DiT-adapted identity reference network,
while closed-source systems such as OmniHuman [ 29 ] extend DiT-based audio-driven generation to full-body animation.
In this work, we distill two such non-causal teachers built on Wan, TalkVerse [ 52 ] (from Wan2.2-5B) for AURA 5B and a 1.3 1.3 B teacher that we train from Wan2.1-1.3B for AURA 1.3B, into causal, few-step streaming students.
blocks.zh:
视频传播模式. 最近的工作进一步扩大了录像制作的传播。 早期的努力如Imagen Video [21], Make-A-Video [43], 调整你的Latents [3], 以及Stable Video Difusion [2] 将图像传播扩展到短片段,一般是通过充气2D架构与时间层. 较近期的开放源代码和工业模式,Sora [ 5],电影Gen [38],Open-Sora [62],CogVideoX [56],HunyuanVideo [27],和Wan [51] ——采用扩散变压器(DiT)架构,在压缩潜伏空间运行,缩放到720 720 p–1080 1080 p分辨率和短片. 这些模型一般是非因果的:它们联合生成整个视频序列超过50个或更多的去诺化步骤,因此不能很好地适应流化应用的耐久性要求. 目前SotA的谈话头型号是基于这种架构. 例如,Hallo3[9]为肖像动画改编了CogVideoX[56],并配有DiT适应的身份参考网络,
而OmniHuman等闭源系统[29]则将基于DiT的音频驱动生成扩展至全身动画.
在这项工作中,我们提炼了Wan、TalkVerse[52](从Wan2.2-5B)为AURA 5B建造的两名非因果教师,以及我们从Wan2.1-1.3B为AURA 1.3B培训的1.3B教师,使之成为因果的、几步流派学生。

blocks.en:
Distillation of Diffusion Models. The slow inference of diffusion models has motivated extensive work on distillation , training a faster few-step student to reproduce a slow
teacher’s output distribution. One particularly successful line is Distribution Matching Distillation
(DMD) [ 58 ] , which trains a one-step student
to minimize the reverse KL to the teacher via a learned critic; DMD2 [ 57 ] extends it to a few-step generator and introduces backward simulation ,
computing the loss on the student’s own rollouts rather than forward-diffused data.
CausVid [ 59 ] applies DMD to distill a
non-causal video teacher into a causal few-step student for streaming
text-to-video. A challenge specific to causal video distillation is the train/test
gap: the student is trained on teacher-provided past frames but must condition on
its own previously generated frames at inference. Self-Forcing [ 23 ] and its variants [ 10 , 64 , 31 , 54 ] address this temporal gap by rolling the student out autoregressively through a
training-time KV cache with stop-gradient. We instead build on DMD2’s backward
simulation [ 57 ] , which exposes
the student to its own denoising trajectory, and adapt it to streaming video
(Sec. 3.4 ) so that the student also conditions on its own past
generations, without maintaining a training-time cache.

blocks.en:
Streaming Talking Heads. A handful of recent works tackle audio-driven talking-head generation in a streaming and few-step setting. Talking Machines ( Low and
Wang, 2025 ) is, to our knowledge, the first to address this regime, distilling a 18 18 B model with DMD and sparse causal attention; weights are not released. Live Avatar ( Huang et al., 2026b ) distills the 14 14 B Wan-S2V model Gao et al. (2025) into a 14 14 B few-step student that runs at 16 16 fps and 480 480 p on a 5 5 -GPU setup. SoulX-FlashTalk ( Shen et al., 2026 ) adopts a similar few-step distillation strategy from a 14 14 B teacher into a 14 14 B student and requires 4 4 GPUs to reach real-time throughput. In contrast, AURA streams on a single GPU: AURA 5B distills a 5 5 B teacher into a same-size causal 4 4 -step student that delivers 720 720 p video at 9.7 9.7 fps, and AURA 1.3B, trained with the same pipeline from our own 1.3 1.3 B teacher, reaches real time at 576 576 p ( 20.7 20.7 fps for a 16 16 Hz playback rate).
Closest to our work is Avatar Forcing ( Cui et al., 2026b ) whose pre-print was concurrently published: It uses a similar DMD-based distillation process but requires a look-ahead window of future audio to generate each frame by design, leading to a small yet incompressible streaming delay.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we present AURA, our two-stage pipeline that distills a non-causal audio-driven video diffusion teacher (TalkVerse) into a 4 4 -step causal student. We first recall Distribution Matching Distillation ( Sec. 3.1 ) and the TalkVerse teacher ( Sec. 3.1 ) to introduce necessary notations and context. Section 3.2 then introduces the causal student and the per-chunk mixed-timestep design that enables a compact KV cache. Section 3.3 and Section 3.4 cover the two training stages, and Section 3.5 finally describes streaming inference.
blocks.zh: 在这一部分,我们介绍AURA, 我们的两阶段管道, 将一个非因果音效驱动的视频传播教师(TalkVerse) 提炼成一个4-4步因果学生。 我们首先回顾《分配与蒸馏相匹配》(第3.1节)和《TalkVerse》教师(第3.1节),介绍必要的标记和背景。 第3.2节随后引入了因果学生和每Chunk混合时间步设计,从而能够实现一个紧凑的KV缓存. 第3.3节和第3.4节涵盖两个培训阶段,第3.5节最后介绍了流派推论。

blocks.en: Backward simulation. Directly applying DMD to multi-step students yields a training-inference mismatch: at training time, the student is fed forward-diffused real samples x t = Ψ ⁡ ( x 0 , t ) x_{t}=\Psi(x_{0},t) , whereas at inference time, intermediate inputs come from previous denoising steps of the student itself. To close this gap, DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024a ) introduces backward simulation . At each training iteration, the student is unrolled for a few denoising steps to produce a synthetic intermediate sample x ^ t \hat{x}_{t} , which then replaces the forward-diffused real sample as input to the DMD objective. Because G θ G_{\theta} is itself a few-step generator, this unrolling is cheap. The DMD gradient and the score-matching update for s gen , η s_{\text{gen},\eta} are then computed at x ^ t \hat{x}_{t} rather than at Ψ ⁡ ( x 0 , t ) \Psi(x_{0},t) , aligning the input distribution seen during training with the one produced at inference. DMD2 also adds a GAN loss on real data. We adopt backward simulation, together with the two time-scale update rule of DMD2, in the second stage of our pipeline ( Sec. 3.4 ), but not the GAN loss: it requires real videos and makes training less stable. The DMD objective alone already brings our student close to its teacher (Sec. 4.3 ).

blocks.en: TalkVerse Architecture. We use TalkVerse Wang et al. (2025) as our teacher model, a 5 5 B-parameter audio-driven video diffusion model built on the Wan2.2-5B Wan et al. (2025) DiT backbone. Its video VAE uses compression factors ( t , h , w ) = ( 4 , 16 , 16 ) (t,h,w)=(4,16,16) , enabling efficient 720 720 p generation. The model is conditioned on a reference identity image, a speech audio track encoded with Wav2Vec2 Baevski et al. (2020) and injected via cross-attention to temporally aligned visual tokens, and a text prompt encoded with T5-XXL Raffel et al. (2020) . Long videos are generated with a sliding-window mechanism that conditions each window on a set of motion frames compressed by a FramePack module Zhang et al. (2026) , and the reference image is assigned a positional offset placed ahead of the denoised window. Inference uses 50 50 denoising steps with a flow-matching solver and classifier-free guidance. We provide a more detailed description in the supplementary material A.1 . TalkVerse is directly the teacher of AURA 5B; for AURA 1.3B, we train a 1.3 1.3 B teacher with the TalkVerse pipeline (Sec. 4.1 and supplementary material A.4 ).

blocks.en: 3.2 AURA Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.2 AURA 结构

blocks.en:
To turn the 50 50 -step bidirectional teacher (TalkVerse) into a 4 4 -step causal student, we introduce three architectural modifications:
chunked causal sliding window attention, removal of motion frames, and per-chunk mixed timesteps. In combination, these changes also enable us to keep a compact rolling KV cache as illustrated in Figure 2 b .
blocks.zh:
为了使50步双向教师(TalkVerse)成为4步4步因果学生,我们进行了三个建筑改造:
块状的因果滑动窗口注意,去除运动框,以及每圆柱混合时间步. 组合起来,这些变化还使我们能够保持一个紧凑的滚动KV缓存,如图2b所示。

blocks.en: Chunked causal attention. The student generates videos in chunks of n c = 4 n_{c}=4 latent frames ( ∼ 0.64 \sim 0.64 s at the 25 25 Hz native rate), whereas the teacher generates 30 30 latent frames ( ∼ 5 \sim 5 s) in a single pass. We enforce causality between chunks in the student: during training, a block-wise causal attention mask prevents frames in chunk C i C_{i} from attending to frames in chunks C j C_{j} for j > i j>i , while attention is bidirectional within a chunk ( Figure 2 a ).
blocks.zh: 引起人们的注意 学生以 n c = 4 n_{c}=4 潜在帧(按 25 Hz 本地利率为 0.64\sim 0.64 s)为单位生成视频,而教师以 单 个通道生成 30 个潜在帧( 5\sim 5 s) 。 我们执行学生中块之间的因果关系:在训练期间,一个块式的因果注意罩使块式C i C_{i}中的帧无法在块式C j C_{j}中为 j > i j>i 参加帧,而注意则在块内双向(图2 a).

blocks.en: No motion frames. TalkVerse normally conditions each generated video sequence on a window of past frames (motion frames) to maintain temporal coherence across windows. In our causal student, the KV cache already carries the past context required for coherence, thus we remove the motion frame mechanism entirely. This also saves us the cost of a few forward passes through the model required to process motion frames for every new chunk.
blocks.zh: 无动画框. TalkVerse 通常每个条件都会在过去的帧(运动帧)窗口上生成视频序列,以保持窗口间的时间一致性. 在我们的因果学生中,KV缓存已经携带了一致性所需的过去上下文,因此我们完全取消了运动帧机制. 这还节省了我们通过处理每个新块的动框所需的模型前进的费用。

blocks.en:
Per-chunk mixed timesteps: a compact KV cache. At 720 720 p, the KV cache is already large at a single noise level due to the high spatial token count per frame. A naive implementation that would scale one (temporal) KV cache per diffusion step would increase the memory cost by the number of denoising steps per chunk. To avoid this, we train the model to handle sequences in which different chunks are at different noise levels: each chunk is assigned a single diffusion timestep t i t_{i} , shared by all frames within the chunk ( Figure 3 , center). This per-chunk mixed timesteps scheme follows CausVid Yin et al. (2025) , which adopts it without explicit motivation. We argue it is a key design choice to enable a compact streaming KV cache.
At inference, the current chunk is fed at a high noise level t curr t_{\mathrm{curr}} while previously generated chunks, cached in the KV cache, are at the lowest noise level reached during their own generation. The cache therefore stores keys and values at a single low noise level per past chunk, rather than at every diffusion step ( Fig. 2(b) ). In contrast, prior streaming audio-driven models that retain multiple noise levels in the cache pay a proportional memory cost Huang et al. (2026b) .
blocks.zh:
Per-chunk混合时间步:一个紧凑的KV缓存. 在720 720 p时,由于每个帧的空间符号计数很高,KV缓存已经是一个单一噪声级的大型. 一个天真的执行,将每个扩散步骤一个(时间)KV缓存分级,将使内存成本增加每个块的去Noing步骤数。 为避免这种情况,我们训练模型处理不同块在不同噪音级别上的序列:每个块被分配到一个单一的扩散时间步 t i t_{i},由块内的所有框架共享(图3,中心). 这个每吨混合时间步方案如下 原因维德 殷等人(2025年),在没有明确动机的情况下采纳. 我们认为,这是一个关键的设计选择,能够使一个紧凑的流式KV缓存。
推论一下,当前块被喂入高噪量的 t curr t_{\mathrm{ curr} 而先前生成的块,缓存在 KV 缓存中, 处于自己生成时达到的最低噪量水平 。 因此,缓存将密钥和值存储在过去块的单个低噪量,而不是每个扩散步骤(图2(b))。 相比之下,在缓存中保留多个噪声水平的前流音频驱动模型则支付比例内存成本黄等人(2026年b).

blocks.en: Figure 3 : Two-stage distillation pipeline . Stage 1 (top, ODE teacher forcing) : the frozen teacher generates a multi-step ODE trajectory from noise to clean latents, conditioned on a reference image, speech audio, and text prompt. A per-chunk mixed timestep state is sampled from this trajectory and fed to the causal student G θ G_{\theta} , which is trained to predict the corresponding clean latents under an MSE loss. Stage 2 (bottom, DMD with backward simulation) : the student generates a video in inference mode without gradients (backward simulation, left), and a per-chunk mixed-timestep state is sampled from its own denoising trajectory. The student is then re-run on this state with gradients enabled, and a DMD loss is computed by comparing the score predicted by a frozen teacher and an online fake score network (right). Gradients flow back through the gradient-enabled student pass only.

blocks.en: 3.3 Stage 1: ODE Teacher Forcing
blocks.zh: 3.3 第一阶段:ODE教师强化

blocks.en: As reported in CausVid Yin et al. (2025) , directly applying DMD to a causal student starting from teacher weights is unstable as the student differs architecturally from the teacher. Therefore, we adapt their ODE-distillation initialization strategy to our setting. Stage 1 trains the causal student to follow the teacher ODE under the new architecture ( Figure 3 , top ), bringing the student close enough to the teacher distribution so that Stage 2 can converge.
blocks.zh: 如CausVid Yin等人(2025年)所报道,直接将DMD应用到一个从教师权重开始的因果学生身上是不稳定的,因为学生在建筑学上与老师不同. 因此,我们调整了他们的ODE-dispiration初始化策略,以适应我们的设定. 第1阶段训练因果学生在新架构下跟随教师ODE(图3,顶部),使学生与教师分布足够接近,以便第2阶段能够汇合.

blocks.en: Training data. We train Stage 1 on our synthetic dataset described in Section 3.6 . Each video comes with latents stored at five timesteps along a 50 50 -step ODE trajectory from the teacher. At training time, the student is queried at the four timesteps { 0.25 , 0.5 , 0.75 , 1 } \{0.25,0.5,0.75,1\} and supervised to predict the clean latent at t = 0 t=0 .
blocks.zh: 培训数据。 我们用3.6节描述的合成数据集来训练第一阶段。 每段录像都有潜伏的画面 沿着老师50步50步的ODE轨迹 保存在五个时段 在训练时,学生在四个时间步处被询问{0.25,0.5,0.75,1}}{0.25,0.5,0.75,1}并被监督预测净潜值为t=0t=0.

blocks.en: Training objective. For each training video, we independently sample a noise level for each chunk uniformly at random from the four cached non-zero timesteps, following the per-chunk mixed timestep scheme of Section 3.2 . This matches the heterogeneous-noise configurations the student encounters at inference, where the current chunk is noisy while past chunks (in the KV cache) are near-clean (at lowest noise level). blocks.en: Backward simulation. A central question in few-step distillation is which samples x ^ 0 \hat{x}_{0} to use when computing the DMD gradient. We adopt the backward simulation strategy of DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024a ) (Sec. 3.1 ) and apply it to our causal, chunked student. At each iteration, we proceed in three steps: (i) we run a full multi-step rollout of G θ G_{\theta} without backpropagation to obtain the intermediate noisy states { x ^ t k } \{\hat{x}_{t_{k}}\} ( t k ∈ { 0.25 , 0.5 , 0.75 , 1 } t_{k}\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75,1\} ) along its own sampling trajectory; (ii) we re-feed these states through G θ G_{\theta} with gradients enabled, using per-chunk mixed timesteps (Sec. 3.2 ) sampled uniformly across the trajectory; (iii) we evaluate the DMD gradient (Eq. 3 ) at the resulting x ^ 0 \hat{x}_{0} ( Figure 3 , bottom ). 3.5 Inference: Causal Generation with rolling KV Cache
blocks.zh: 3.5 国家 推论: 带有滚动 KV 快取的因果生成

blocks.en:
At inference, the student generates the video autoregressively, one chunk of 4 4 latent frames at a time, in 4 4 diffusion steps per chunk. Within each chunk, we adopt the predict-and-renoise scheme of DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024a ) (see supplementary material A.2 ).
To extend generation to longer sequences, we use a rolling KV cache with a first-chunk anchor that provides temporal context across chunks, and a RoPE Su et al. (2024) re-indexing scheme that bridges training and inference.

为了将生成扩展到更长的序列,我们使用一个滚动的KV缓存,其中有一个第一重锚,提供跨块的时间背景,以及一个ROPE Su等人. (2024) 搭桥培训和推论的重新索引计划.

blocks.en:
Rolling KV cache. The sampling scheme of DMD2 describes the denoising of a single chunk. To generate longer videos, each new chunk must attend to previously generated chunks for temporal coherence. A naive KV cache that stores keys and values for all previously generated chunks would grow linearly with video length. We instead use a rolling cache of fixed size matching our sliding window attention training: 1. the first chunk is kept as a fixed anchor that subsequent chunks always attend to. This mirrors the attention sink mechanism used to stabilize streaming language models ( Xiao et al., 2024 ) and also often adopted for streaming long-video generation ( Liu et al., 2026 ) ; 2. the latest n n chunks ( n = 1 n=1 in our setting), which provide the immediate temporal context for local motion continuity. We keep a single past chunk ( n = 1 n=1 ): enlarging the window to n = 2 n=2 does not improve quality overall 
while increasing cache size and lowering throughput (supplementary material, Table 11 ). All other chunks are evicted from the cache once they fall outside this window,
which yields constant inference memory regardless of video duration. Moreover,
thanks to the per-chunk mixed-timestep training described in Section 3.2 , cached entries only
need to store keys and values at the lowest noise level reached at the last
denoising step of the chunk, rather than at every diffusion step. The same
attention pattern is reproduced at training time by the block-causal mask
( Figure 2(a) ), in a single forward pass
and without maintaining a KV cache.

RoPE indexing. At inference, generated-frame positions grow without bound, while the reference frame is anchored at a fixed temporal RoPE position 10 10 to 40 40 latents ahead of the current generation front at training time ( Section 3.1 and supplementary material A.1 ). To preserve this training-time configuration, we explore a scheme to re-index the reference every 30 30 new generated latent frames, in the spirit of the re-indexed reference or sink frames of recent streaming avatar models Huang et al. (2026b) ; Li et al. (2026) ; Cui et al. (2026b) , shifting it by + 30 +30 each time so that its offset relative to the generation front cycles between + 40 +40 and + 10 +10 ( Figure 8 in supplementary material). This keeps the relative position of the reference within the regime the model was trained on, and avoids the position drift that would otherwise accumulate over long autoregressive rollouts.
In practice, we find that this reindexing design helps stabilizing long generation for AURA 5B. For the smaller AURA 1.3B however, it is more beneficial to directly cap the RoPE positions of the generated frames to the range seen in training in our experiments, as Anchor Forcing Yang et al. (2026) and StreamAvatar Sun et al. (2026) do (supplementary material A.4 ).

在实践中,我们发现这种重新索引设计有助于稳定AURA 5B的长生成. 然而,对于较小的AURA 1.3B来说,将生成框架的ROPE位置直接限制在我们实验中训练中看到的范围更为有益,如Anchor Forcing Yang等人(2026年)和StrevAvatar Sun等人(2026年)所做的那样(补充材料A.4.)。

blocks.en: 3.6 Synthetic Talking-Head Dataset
blocks.zh: 3.6 合成对讲-头数据集

blocks.en: We find that existing audio-driven video datasets are ill-suited to our training setup: the TalkVerse training set is released only as YouTube URLs and is difficult to obtain reliably, while the Hallo3 dataset Cui et al. (2025) contains clips too short to match our teacher’s single-chunk generation window of ∼ 5 \sim 5 s. We instead build a synthetic dataset by running the TalkVerse teacher on conditioning inputs we control, and release it to support Stage 1 ODE teacher forcing ( Section 3.3 ) and future work on audio-driven distillation.
blocks.zh: 我们发现现有的音频驱动视频数据集不适合我们的培训设置:TalkVerse培训集仅作为YouTube URL发布,难以可靠获取,而Hallo3数据集Cui等人. 校对:Soup 相反,我们通过运行TalkVerse的教师来构建一个关于我们所控制投入的合成数据集,并发布该数据集以支持第一阶段ODE教师强迫(第3.3节)和今后关于音频驱动蒸馏的工作。

blocks.en: Conditioning inputs. We draw reference images and their associated text prompts from Hallo3 dataset ( Cui et al., 2025 ) , and pair each (image, prompt) to a synthetic speech track: We first obtain textual English audio transcripts of Youtube videos provided in the LiveCC dataset Chen et al. (2025) . Then, we generate speech from a subset of these transcript using an off-the-shelf text-to-speech model Zeghidour et al. (2025) . The resulting clips average 4.8 4.8 s, matching the teacher’s chunk size.
blocks.zh: 有条件的投入. 我们从Hallo3数据集(Cui等人,2025年)中绘制参考图像及其相关文本提示,并逐一对(图像,即时)合成语音轨道: 我们首先获得LiveCC数据集Chen等人(2025年)提供的Youtube视频的英文文字录音记录。 然后,我们用现成的文本对语音模型Zeghidour et al.(2025)从这些语录的子集中生成语音. 结果的剪辑平均为4.8 4.8 s,与教师的块大小相匹配。

blocks.en:
Video generation. For each (image, prompt, audio) triplet, we run the TalkVerse teacher at 720 720 p and 25 25 Hz with 50 50 ODE steps and a guidance scale of 4.5 4.5 . Reference image quality is heterogeneous across Hallo3, which also leads to diverse quality in the resulting video clips; No quality filtering is applied.
For each generated video, we also store the teacher’s latent ODE trajectory at five timesteps: the initial noise ( t = 1 t=1 ), three intermediate states ( t ∈ { 0.75 , 0.5 , 0.25 } t\in\{0.75,0.5,0.25\} ), and the final clean latent ( t = 0 t=0 ). Latents follow the TalkVerse VAE compression ( 4 × 16 × 16 4{\times}16{\times}16 over time and space). We additionally store the decoded clean videos as MP4 files alongside the original audio tracks.
blocks.zh:
视频生成. 对于每个(图像,即时,音频)三进制,我们以720 720 p和25 25 Hz运行TalkVerse教师,有50个ODE步骤,指导尺度为4.54.5. 参考图像质量在Hallo3各处不尽相同,这也导致所产生的录像片段质量不一; 没有采用质量过滤。
对于每个生成的视频,我们也存储教师潜伏的ODE轨迹在五个时间步:初始噪声(t = 1 t = 1),三个中间状态(t { { 0.75, 0. 5, 0. 25 } t\\ 0.75, 0. 5, 0. 25 }),以及最终的清洁潜伏(t = 0 t = 0). Latents跟随TalkVerse VAE压缩(4×16×16 4×times}16×times}16随着时间和空间). 我们额外将解码的干净视频作为MP4文件与原始音频音轨一起存储.

blocks.en: Release. The final dataset totals 30,000 30{,}000 clips ( 38.7 38.7 h of synthetic videos, compared to ∼ 70 \sim 70 h for Hallo3 and CelebV). We release the audio tracks, decoded videos, and the five-timestep latent ODE trajectories to foster reproducibility and future work on talking heads generation. TalkVerse is only available at 5 5 B parameters. Since its training code is open source, we reuse its training pipeline to train our own 1.3 1.3 B bidirectional teacher on a smaller Wan2.1 backbone (Sec. 4.1 ), which serves as the teacher of AURA 1.3B. We also release its weights and the 30 30 K ODE trajectories it generated for Stage 1 of AURA 1.3B (Sec. A.4 ).

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
We train two students with the same recipe, building on the open-source TalkVerse codebase for training and inference. AURA 5B is initialized from its teacher, TalkVerse Wang et al. (2025) ( 5 5 B parameters, built on Wan2.2 5 5 B). AURA 1.3B is initialized from a 1.3 1.3 B bidirectional speech-to-video teacher that we train ourselves with the TalkVerse training pipeline, adapting Wan2.1 1.3 1.3 B text-to-video Wan et al. (2025) to speech as TalkVerse does from Wan2.2 5 5 B, with LoRA adapters on the backbone and audio cross-attention layers. This teacher differs from TalkVerse in two ways. It is trained on much less data: 31 31 h of real Hallo3 video ( 23 23 K clips), whereas TalkVerse is trained for about one epoch on its 6.3 6.3 K-hour dataset. Its audio features come from the Mimi speech codec Défossez et al. (2024) instead of Wav2Vec2: Mimi is a more recent codec with a causal, streaming encoder, and we keep its first, semantic level (Sec. A.4 of the supplementary material).
Both students are trained with LoRA adapters Hu et al. (2022) of rank 128 128 on the attention layers. We additionally unfreeze their timestep embedding and output head, since our models use the per-chunk mixed-timestep scheme of Section 3.2 rather than the single shared timestep of the teachers. Both generate video in chunks of n c = 4 n_{c}=4 latent frames with 4 4 diffusion denoising steps per chunk. They differ in output resolution and rate: AURA 5B generates 720 720 p video ( 1216 × 768 1216\times 768 or 960 × 960 960\times 960 , depending on the aspect ratio of the reference) played back at 25 25 Hz, the native output rate of TalkVerse, and AURA 1.3B generates 576 576 p video ( 768 × 512 768\times 512 or 576 × 576 576\times 576 , likewise) played back at 16 16 Hz, the native rate of Wan2.1; we use fps (frames per second) elsewhere to denote throughput. Unless stated otherwise, experiments use AURA 5B.

blocks.en: Two-stage LoRA training. Each stage trains its own LoRA adapters. At the end of Stage 1 (ODE teacher forcing), its LoRA is merged into the base weights, and Stage 2 (DMD with backward simulation) trains a fresh LoRA of the same rank, avoiding stacked adapters. The Stage 2 critic is initialized from the teacher, and only its LoRA adapters are trained. Both models use batch size 256 256 and 5 5 critic updates per student update. AURA 5B runs Stage 1 for 120 120 K steps at learning rate 1e-5 and Stage 2 for 5 5 K steps at 3.5e-7 , on 64 64 H100 GPUs. AURA 1.3B runs Stage 1 for 40 40 K steps at 1e-5 , on trajectories of its own teacher, and Stage 2 for 6.5 6.5 K steps at 2e-7 , on 32 32 H100 GPUs. Other hyperparameters, including the 1.3B teacher’s, are in the supplementary material (Sec. A.3 , A.4 ).
blocks.zh: 两阶段LORA训练. 每个阶段都训练自己的LORA适配器. 在第1阶段(ODE teacher force)结束时,它的LORA被合并为基重,第2阶段(DMD带有后向模拟)训练一个同样等级的新鲜LORA,避免堆叠适配器. "阶段2"评论员从老师处初始化,只有它的LORA适配器接受了训练. 两种模式都使用批量大小256 256和5个评论家更新每个学生更新. AURA 5B按学习速率1e-5的120 120 K步运行第1阶段,按3.5e-7的5 5 K步运行第2阶段,在64 64个H100 GPU上运行。 AURA 1.3B在自己的老师的轨迹上为40个40K步运行第1阶段,在2e-7运行第2阶段为6.5K步,在32个32个H100 GPU运行。 其他超参数,包括1.3B教师的参数,都在补充材料中(Sec.A.3、A.4)。

blocks.en:
Baselines. We compare AURA against four open-source audio-driven avatar generation models. TalkVerse Wang et al. (2025) , our teacher, serves as a high-quality reference for the distillation. Wan-S2V 14B Gao et al. (2025) and Hallo3 Cui et al. (2025) are two recent large-scale non-causal S2V model. Live Avatar Huang et al. (2026b) is a streaming few-step approach and the closest competitor to AURA in inference regime.
For all baselines we use the authors’ released code and checkpoints, and run inference under each method’s recommended settings.

对于所有基线,我们使用作者发布的代码和检查站,并在每种方法推荐的设置下进行推断。

blocks.en: Quality and identity. In Table 1 and 2 we report our main quantitative comparison against all baselines, alongside model size, output resolution, and number of diffusion steps. Despite using only 4 4 denoising steps instead of 50 50 , AURA matches or improves on its TalkVerse teacher across most automatic metrics, and is comparable to the much larger Wan-S2V ( 14 14 B, multi-step) on FVD, JEDi, and audio–visual alignment. On identity preservation (CSIM), AURA outperforms all baselines on both test sets ( 0.79 0.79 for AURA 5B and 0.84 0.84 for AURA 1.3B on Hallo3 test , 0.72 0.72 and 0.77 0.77 on CelebV-HQ test ), which we attribute to our RoPE indexing schemes ( Sec. 3.5 ) and to keeping the initial generated chunks in the rolling cache, both of which limit identity drift over long generations.
blocks.zh: 质量与身份. 在表1和表2中,我们报告我们与所有基线的主要数量比较,以及模型大小、产出分辨率和传播步骤的数目。 尽管AURA只使用4个调试步骤而不是50个调试步骤,但AURA在TalkVerse的教师身上比对或改进了大多数自动度量衡,与FVD、JEDi和视听校对方面更大的Wan-S2V(14 14 B,多步)相当。 关于身份保全(CSIM),AURA在两个测试组上都超过了所有基线(AURA 5B为0.79 0.79,HALLO3测试为0.84 0.84 AURA 1.3B,CELBV-HQ测试为0.72 0.72和0.77 0.77),我们将此归因于我们的RoPE指数化计划(第3.5条),并将最初产生的块保留在滚动缓存中,两者都限制了身份漂移在远代。

blocks.en:
Speed. Both AURA models are faster than all baselines, including Live Avatar, which is also a few-step model. Throughputs are reported in raw frames per second. AURA 5B, TalkVerse and Hallo3 generate at 25 25 Hz, Live Avatar, Wan-S2V and AURA 1.3B at 16 16 Hz. Measured in generated seconds of video per second of compute, AURA’s lead over the latter two is larger
still. AURA 5B runs the end-to-end pipeline at 9.7 9.7 fps on a single H 100 100 , a ∼ 𝟏𝟕 × \mathbf{\sim 17\times} speedup over its TalkVerse teacher ( 0.58 0.58 fps); its diffusion transformer and VAE decoder alone reach 19.7 19.7 and 22.7 22.7 fps (on the DiT, a ∼ 𝟑𝟎 × \mathbf{\sim 30\times} speedup over the teacher’s 0.69 0.69 fps), and the end-to-end throughput is bounded by their sequential composition. AURA 1.3B runs at 20.7 20.7 fps end-to-end ( 28.8 28.8 fps for the DiT, 96.9 96.9 fps for the VAE decoder), faster than its 16 16 Hz playback rate: it streams in real time on a single H 100 100 , a ∼ 𝟐𝟑 × \mathbf{\sim 23\times} speedup over its bidirectional teacher ( 0.90 0.90 fps, measured on a single 4.8 4.8 s window since this teacher generates fixed-length clips). These timings use the square reference of our protocol ( 576 × 576 576\times 576 output); at 768 × 512 768\times 512 , AURA 1.3B runs at 17.3 17.3 fps end-to-end, still faster than real time. Figure 1 (right) summarizes the quality–speed trade-off: AURA matches the best baselines on quality while being one to two orders of magnitude faster. Figure 6 in the supplementary material adds complementary visualizations.

Speed速. 两个AURA模型都比所有基线都快,包括Live Avatar,这也是一个几步模型. 吞吐量以原始框架每秒报告。 AURA 5B、TalkVerse 和 Halo3 以 25 Hz 、 Live Avatar 、 Wan-S2V 和 AURA 1.3 B 16 Hz 生成。
还行 AURA 5B在单机H 100 100上以9.7 9.7英尺的速度运行端对端管道,在TalkVerse教师(0.58 0.58英尺)上以 17 × mathbf\sim 17\tim 17\tim的速度运行;其扩散变压器和VAE解码器单机达到19.7 19.7 和 22.7 22.7英尺(在DiT上, a 30 × mathbf\sim 30\tim 30\tim)的速度超过教师的 0.69 0.69 0.69英尺),端到端的吞吐量以它们的顺序组成为界. AURA 1.3B运行于20.7 20.7 fps 端对端(DiT为28.8 28.8 fps,VAE解码器为96.9 fps),比其16 Hz回放速率快:在单H 100 100 上实时流出 23 × mathbf\sim 23\times) 速度超双向教师(0.90 0.90 fps,在单4.8 s 窗口上测量,因为这位教师产生固定长片段). 这些时间使用我们协议的正方形参考(576×576576\times 576输出);在768×512 768\times 512时,AURA 1.3B运行于17.3 17.3英尺的端对端,仍然比实时快. 图1(右)总结了质量-速度的权衡:AURA在质量上符合最佳基线,同时更快地达到一至两个数量级。 补充材料中的图6增加了补充可视化.

blocks.en: Long-form streaming stability. A central claim of AURA is that its rolling KV cache sustains generation over an unbounded stream at constant memory. To measure how quality and identity evolve over time, we run both models ( 4 4 steps) on the 100 100 Hallo3 test references driven by 60 60 s of speech and compute metrics on consecutive 10 10 s segments ( Figure 7 and Table 10 in the supplementary material). For AURA 1.3B, FVD and lip-sync stay flat over the six segments (FVD 179 179 – 186 186 , Sync-C 4.73 4.73 – 4.81 4.81 , no segment significantly different from the first), and so does identity for most videos (median per-video CSIM change − 0.02 -0.02 over the minute; a few videos drift and pull the mean from 0.83 0.83 to 0.78 0.78 ). AURA 5B degrades slightly after the first segment (FVD from 182 182 to 195 195 – 206 206 , then stable) and its identity drifts slightly (CSIM from 0.76 0.76 to 0.69 0.69 ).
blocks.zh: 长式流线稳定. AURA的一个中心主张是,其滚动的KV缓存在恒定内存的无约束流上维持生成. 为了衡量质量和身份如何随时间演变,我们在100个100个Hallo3测试参考文献上运行两个模型(4个步骤),由连续10个部分的60个语音和计算指标驱动(补充材料中图7和表10)。 对于AURA 1.3B, FVD和唇音在六个片段(FVD 179 – 186 186,Sync-C 4.73 4.73 – 4.81 4.81,与第一个片段没有明显区别)上保持平整,大多数视频的身份也一样(每集视频的中间值变化为-02-0.02;少数视频漂移并拉出平均值从0.83 0.83到0.78 0.78)。 AURA 5B在第一段(FVD从182 182到195 195 – 206 206,然后稳定)和其身份漂移(CSIM从0.76 0.76到0.69 0.69)后略有降解.

blocks.en:
Perceptual quality. Distribution-based metrics (FID, FVD, JEDi) capture global feature statistics but do not penalize certain local artifacts: Hallo3 obtains the best FID, FVD, and JEDi on both test sets, yet its generations exhibit exaggerated mouth motion and recurrent hand artifacts that these metrics fail to flag (qualitative analysis in Fig. 9 , supplementary material). To assess perceived quality directly, we run an anonymous human evaluation on the Mabyduck platform. We collected 400 400 pairwise comparisons from 27 27 raters on the 100 100 Hallo3 test clips, covering all pairs among AURA 5B, AURA 1.3B, Hallo3 and our TalkVerse teacher, along four axes: overall visual quality, lip-sync, reference fidelity, and naturalness. Results are aggregated into per-axis Bayesian Elo scores ( Fig. 4 ). Both AURA models are preferred over Hallo3 on all four axes, confirming that
Hallo3’s distribution-metric lead does not translate into perceived quality. Against the non-causal 50 50 -step teacher, AURA 5B ranks higher on reference fidelity, consistent with our CSIM results, and is on par on visual quality, lip-sync and naturalness, despite being causal and ∼ 17 × \sim\!17\times faster. AURA 1.3B also ranks above TalkVerse on reference fidelity, but below AURA 5B and TalkVerse on visual quality, which reflects its lower resolution, as well as on lip-sync and naturalness.
blocks.zh:
知觉质性. 基于分配的衡量标准(FID、FVD、JEDI)收集全球特征统计数据,但不惩罚某些当地文物: Halo3在两套测试中都获得了最好的FID,FVD和JEDi,然而其世代表现出夸张的口部运动和反复出现的手部文物,这些度量衡未能标出(Fig. 9中的定性分析,补充材料). 为了直接评估所感知的质量,我们在Mabyduck平台上进行了一次匿名的人类评估. 我们从100个Hallo3测试片段的27个27个评分中收集了400 400个对比,涵盖了AURA 5B、AURA 1.3B、Hallo3和我们的TalkVerse教师之间的所有对比,沿四个轴线:整体视觉质量、唇拍、参考忠诚和自然。 结果汇总为每轴Bayesian Elo分数(图4)。 在所有四个轴上,两个AURA模型都比Hallo3更受青睐,证实
Halo3的分布度测定铅没有转化为感知的质量. AURA 5B在参考忠诚度方面排名较高, 17秒快一点 AURA 1.3B在参考忠诚度上也排在TalkVerse以上,但在视觉质量上则排在AURA 5B和TalkVerse以下,这反映了它的低分辨率,以及唇和自然性.

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablations
blocks.zh: 4.3 违约

blocks.en: We ablate the main design choices of our method. Unless stated otherwise, all ablations use the 5B student trained on the full pipeline and are evaluated on the Hallo3 test set with the same 10 10 s clips as the main results (Sec. 4.2 ); the 4 4 -step default row of each ablation is the AURA 5B row of Tab. 1 . We add two diagnostics, defined in Sec. A.9 of the supplementary material: Sharp. , the variance of the Laplacian of the aligned face (frame-level sharpness proxies are dominated by background and noise), and Δ \Delta Col. , a within-clip colour drift: how much further the mean colour of the face moves away from that of the reference face (distance in CIELAB) between the first ( 0.5 0.5 – 2.5 2.5 s) and last ( 7.5 7.5 – 9.5 9.5 s) two seconds.
blocks.zh: 我们放弃我们方法的主要设计选择。 除非另有说明,否则所有烧伤都使用在全管道上训练的5B学生,并在Hallo3测试集上进行评估,主要结果为10个10个短片(第4.2节);每根烧伤的4个4步默认行是Tab的AURA 5B行. 1,我们增加了两个诊断,在补充材料的Sec.A.9中定义:Sharp.,对齐面的拉普拉西安差异(框架级的锐度代号以背景和噪音为主),和\\Delta Col.,一个内侧颜色漂移:第一秒(0.5 - 2.5 s)和最后一秒(7.5 - 9.5 s)之间,脸的正色与参考面(CIELAB中的距离)相去多远。

blocks.en:
Number of diffusion steps. Table 3 reports quality metrics when generating each chunk in { 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } \{1,2,3,4\} diffusion steps. Visually, videos become blurrier as the number of steps decreases (Sec. 4.4 ), which distribution metrics barely capture: FVD and JEDi are best at 4 4 steps and degrade only slightly at 3 3 and 2 2 steps, FID is even marginally better at 3 3 and 2 2 steps, and all drop clearly at 1 1 step. Face sharpness makes the blur explicit: it decreases monotonically from 50.4 50.4 at 4 4 steps to 37.5 37.5 , 36.5 36.5 and 27.0 27.0 at 3 3 , 2 2 and 1 1 steps. Identity (CSIM) and lip-sync remain essentially stable down to 2 2 steps; the lower warping error with fewer steps reflects the same blur, which leaves fewer details to flag as inconsistent across frames, rather than a real improvement.
We adopt 4 4 steps in all other experiments as the best trade-off between per-frame quality and inference speed.

blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We present AURA, a family of causal few-step speech-to-video models for streaming
talking-head generation. Distilling a bidirectional teacher into a same-size 4 4 -step causal student through a two-stage pipeline and a rolling KV cache, AURA 5B
matches or improves on its TalkVerse teacher on FVD and JEDi at a 17 × 17\times speedup, delivering 720 720 p video at 9.7 9.7 fps on a single GPU. AURA 1.3B, distilled with the same pipeline from a 1.3 1.3 B teacher, streams 576 576 p video in real time on a single GPU ( 20.7 20.7 fps for a 16 16 Hz playback rate). We also release a 30,000 30{,}000 -clip
synthetic dataset with teacher ODE trajectories, as well as our 1.3 1.3 B teacher and its ODE trajectories, to support future work on
audio-driven distillation.

blocks.en: A.1 TalkVerse
blocks.zh: A.1 讲义

blocks.en: We use TalkVerse Wang et al. (2025) as the teacher of AURA 5B, a 5B-parameter audio-driven video generation model built on the Wan2.2-5B Wan et al. (2025) Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone, originally pretrained for text-and-image-to-video generation. TalkVerse extends the Wan-S2V Gao et al. (2025) design for speech-conditioned video synthesis to the Wan2.2 backbone, and trades the 14B-parameter scale of Wan-S2V for a smaller 5B model, trained on a high-resolution open-source dataset.
blocks.zh: 我们使用TalkVerse Wang et al. (2025)作为AURA 5B的老师,这是基于Wan2.2-5B的5B参数音频视频生成模型 Wan 等 (英语). (2025)传播变形器(DiT)骨干,最初为文字和图像到视频生成而预训. 说话 Wanse 扩展了 Wan -S2V 范围 Gao et al. (2025) 语音条件视频合成设计到Wan2.2主干线,将Wan-S2V的14B参数尺度换成更小的5B模型,经过高分辨率开源数据集培训.

blocks.en: Latent space. TalkVerse uses the Wan2.2 video VAE, which downsamples by ( t , h , w ) = ( 4 , 16 , 16 ) (t,h,w)=(4,16,16) , a higher compression ratio than the ( 4 , 8 , 8 ) (4,8,8) commonly used in prior video diffusion models (e.g. Wan2.1). This yields a 4 × 4\times reduction in latent token count at the same resolution, enabling efficient high-resolution (720p) generation.
blocks.zh: 深层空间。 说话 Verse使用Wan2.2视频VAE,它通过(t,h,w) = (4,16,w) = (4,h,w) = (4,16,16) 的下标,压缩比高于(4,8,8) 以往视频传播模型(如Wan2.1)常用的(4,8,8). 这导致同一分辨率的潜在符号计数减少4×4\次,从而能够高效的高分辨率(720p)生成。

blocks.en: Conditioning. The model is conditioned on three inputs: (i) a reference identity image, (ii) a speech audio track, and (iii) a text prompt describing the video content. Audio is encoded with Wav2Vec2 Baevski et al. (2020) and injected into a subset of DiT blocks via cross-attention from visual tokens to audio tokens, with each latent frame attending to a temporally aligned audio segment. The text prompt is encoded with T5-XXL Raffel et al. (2020) and injected through cross-attention. TalkVerse is trained on the large-scale TalkVerse-2.3M dataset of high-resolution audio-synchronized clips.
blocks.zh: 条件 该模型以三种输入为条件: (一)参考身份图像, (二)语音音频音轨, (三)文字提示描述视频内容. 音频与Wav2Vec2 Baevski等人(2020年)编码,通过视觉符号到音频符号的交叉意向注入到DiT块的子集中,每个潜在帧都处理一个时间对齐的音频段. 文字提示符与T5-XXL Raffel et al. (2020)编码,通过交叉注解注入. TalkVerse接受了高分辨率音频同步剪辑的大型TalkVerse-2.3M数据集的培训.

blocks.en: Long-video generation: temporal context. To generate minute-long videos, TalkVerse uses a sliding-window mechanism: each window denoises a fixed number of frames conditioned on a window of preceding frames, referred to as motion frames . To keep the token budget tractable, the motion frames are compressed by a FramePack module Zhang et al. (2026) and assigned negative positional embeddings to mark them as past context.
blocks.zh: 长视频生成:时间背景. 为了生成分钟的视频,TalkVerse使用滑动窗口机制:每个窗口都会对固定数量的帧进行修饰,以前一个帧的窗口为条件,称为运动帧. 为了保持符号预算的可拉动性,运动帧被一个FramePack模块Zhang等人(2026年)压缩,并指定负位嵌入,将其标记为过去上下文.

blocks.en: Long-video generation: reference frame placement. The reference identity image is assigned a positional embedding placed after the denoised video window, specifically position 40 40 for a denoised window of 30 30 latent frames. This forward offset makes the model “chase” the reference rather than copy it, which the authors report avoids copy-paste artifacts and looped body movements when the same reference is reused across sliding windows.
blocks.zh: 长视频生成:参考框架布置. 参考身份图像被分配到一个位置嵌入式,放置在解密视频窗口之后,具体来说是40-40的位置,用于30个潜在帧的解密窗口。 这一向前冲抵使模型“查抄”成为参考文献而不是复制文献,作者们报告说,当同一参考文献在滑动窗口重复使用时,避免复制复制文物和循环体运动。

blocks.en: Training and inference. TalkVerse is trained with LoRA on the DiT attention layers, while audio projection, audio cross-attention, and FramePack-related modules are fully fine-tuned. Inference uses 50 denoising steps with a flow-matching solver and classifier-free guidance.
blocks.zh: 训练与推论. TalkVerse与LORA一起接受DiT关注层的培训,而音频投影,音频交叉关注,以及FramePack相关模块则完全微调. 推论使用50个带有流量匹配解析器和无分解器导线的解析步骤.

blocks.en: Within each chunk, we adopt the predict-and-renoise scheme of DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024a ) . Standard flow matching integration z t − Δ ​ t = z t + v θ ​ ( z t , t , c ) ⋅ Δ ​ t z_{t-\Delta t}=z_{t}+v_{\theta}(z_{t},t,c)\cdot\Delta t assumes that intermediate states lie on the learned ODE trajectory, an assumption that breaks down in the few-step regime, where each step spans a large interval of noise levels. Given a schedule of K = 4 K=4 denoising steps with timesteps 1 = t 0 > t 1 > ⋯ > t K = 0 1=t_{0}>t_{1}>\cdots>t_{K}=0 , the chunk is initialized as z t 0 ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , I ) z_{t_{0}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I) , and each step k k proceeds in two parts. The student first predicts the velocity v θ ​ ( z t k , t k , c ) v_{\theta}(z_{t_{k}},t_{k},c) and reconstructs an estimate of the clean latent under the linear flow matching parameterization: x ^ 0 ( k ) = z t k − t k ⋅ v θ ​ ( z t k , t k , c ) . \hat{x}_{0}^{(k)}=z_{t_{k}}-t_{k}\cdot v_{\theta}(z_{t_{k}},t_{k},c). (4) This estimate is then re-noised to the next noise level t k + 1 t_{k+1} with fresh Gaussian noise ϵ ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , I ) \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I) : z t k + 1 = ( 1 − t k + 1 ) ⋅ x ^ 0 ( k ) + t k + 1 ⋅ ϵ . z_{t_{k+1}}=(1-t_{k+1})\cdot\hat{x}_{0}^{(k)}+t_{k+1}\cdot\epsilon. (5) The final latent of the chunk is x ^ 0 = x ^ 0 ( K − 1 ) \hat{x}_{0}=\hat{x}_{0}^{(K-1)} , obtained at the last denoising step. The re-noising in Eq. 5 projects each intermediate estimate back onto the manifold of noisy latents the student was trained on, rather than following a straight-line integration of the velocity field. The same scheme is used during Stage 2 training to roll out the student without backpropagation and produce the noisy states { x ^ t k } \{\hat{x}_{t_{k}}\} used by backward simulation (Sec. 3.4 ), keeping training and inference aligned.

blocks.en: Teacher. The bidirectional teacher is trained with flow matching on 23,147 23{,}147 real Hallo3 Cui et al. The loss is a flow-matching MSE weighted by face and body masks, and the audio, image and text conditions are each dropped with probability 0.1 0.1 for classifier-free guidance. We use the checkpoint at 60 60 K steps. Unlike TalkVerse, the teacher has no motion frames (no FramePack module): it is only used for distillation, which requires single 20 20 -latent windows, so it never has to extend a video beyond one window.

blocks.en: Stage 1 data. Since the teacher is trained on real Hallo3 videos, we build its ODE trajectories on 30 30 K Hallo3 conditions (first frame, the clip’s own speech, and its caption, or the generic prompt “a person is talking” for 61 % 61\% of them), disjoint from Hallo3 test , with 50 50 ODE steps and a guidance scale of 4.5 4.5 .
blocks.zh: 第一阶段数据。 因为老师接受过真实的Hallo3视频的训练,所以我们在30 K Hallo3条件下构建了ODE的轨迹(第一帧,片段自己的演讲和标题,或者61 % 的 61 % 的 通用即时“一个人在说话 ” ) , 与Hallo3测试脱节,有50个ODE步骤和4.5 的指针。

blocks.en: Stage 1 and Stage 2. Stage 1 regresses the teacher trajectories as for AURA 5B, with the clean timestep t = 0 t=0 included among the per-chunk timesteps, and LoRA adapters on the attention layers and on the audio layers. Stage 2 uses DMD with backward simulation on 92 92 K conditions (Hallo3 first frames and prompts paired with synthetic speech from the pipeline of Sec. 3.6 , disjoint from Hallo3 test ); the student audio adapters are frozen, and the generator is read from an exponential moving average of its weights (decay 0.99 0.99 ). We keep the EMA checkpoint at 6,500 6{,}500 optimizer steps. At inference, AURA 1.3B uses the 4 4 -step schedule of AURA 5B and re-indexes the RoPE positions of the generated frames so that they never exceed the range seen during training.
blocks.zh: 第一阶段和阶段 2. 第1阶段将教师的轨迹与AURA 5B的轨迹相倒退,将干净的时步 t = 0 t = 0 列入每个时步,并将LORA适配器列入注意力层和音频层。 第2阶段使用DMD在92 92 K条件下进行反向模拟(Hallo3第一帧和提示与Sec3.6管道的合成语音对齐,与Hallo3测试脱节);学生的音频适配器被冷却,生成器从其重量的指数移动平均值(decay 0.99 0.99)读取. 我们把EMA检查站保持在6500 6{,}500个优化步骤。 推论AURA 1.3B采用AURA 5B的4-4步表,并重新索引生成帧的ROPE位置,以便它们不会超过训练时看到的范围.

blocks.en: A.9 Diagnostic metrics for the ablations

blocks.en: The ablations (Sec. 4.3 ) use two diagnostics in addition to the metrics of Sec. 4.1 , computed on the 100 100 Hallo3 test clips ( 10 10 s) and averaged over videos.
blocks.zh: 除了Sec.4.1的度量标准外,用两种诊断法(第4.3条)计算出100个Hallo3测试片段(10 10 s),并平均通过视频进行。

blocks.en: Face sharpness (Sharp.) Variance of the 3 × 3 3{\times}3 Laplacian, a standard focus measure Pech-Pacheco et al. (2000) , on the grey-level inner face (brows to chin, cheek to cheek). At 5 5 frames per second, the largest face (RetinaFace Deng et al. (2020) , ResNet-50) is aligned on the ArcFace Deng et al. (2022) template at 256 × 256 256{\times}256 , so that its size does not depend on the output resolution; frames without a face are skipped. Higher is sharper. We do not use the whole frame: frame-level proxies (variance of the Laplacian, high-frequency FFT energy) are dominated by background texture and noise, and rank the 1 1 -step and Stage-1-only models as the sharpest.
blocks.zh: 面尖(夏尔普). 3×3 3 3×times}3 Laplacian,一种标准聚焦度量法Pech-Pacheco等人(2000年),在灰色的内侧面(眉到下巴,颊到颊)上的差异. 在每秒5帧时,最大面(RetinaFace Deng et al. (2020),ResNet-50)在ArcFace Deng et al. (2022)模板上对齐,为256×256~256{\times}256,因此其大小不取决于输出分辨率;没有面的帧会被跳过. 高处更锋利. 我们不使用整个帧:帧级的代位(拉普拉西安变位,高频FFT能量)以背景纹理和噪声为主,将11阶和阶段1型列为最尖端的型号.

blocks.en: Colour drift ( Δ \Delta Col.) How much further the face colour moves away from the reference over a clip. At 5 5 frames per second, we compute Δ ​ E \Delta E , the CIELAB distance between the mean colour of the inner face (detected and aligned as above, at 112 × 112 112{\times}112 ) and that of the reference face. Δ \Delta Col. is the mean Δ ​ E \Delta E over the last two seconds ( 7.5 7.5 – 9.5 9.5 s) minus the mean over the first two ( 0.5 0.5 – 2.5 2.5 s); lower is better. This follows the start-versus-end drift measure of FramePack Zhang et al. (2026) and Rolling Forcing Liu et al. (2026) , restricted to the face and taken against the reference, hence signed. For scale, a Δ ​ E \Delta E of about 2.3 2.3 is commonly taken as a just-noticeable difference Mahy et al. (1994) : the default model stays at Δ ​ E ≈ 2 \Delta E\approx 2 from the reference ( Δ \Delta Col. 0.4 0.4 ), whereas the t = 50 t{=}50 refresh variants drift by 3.1 3.1 , to 5.7 5.7 – 5.8 5.8 .

blocks.en: A.10 Rolling cache window size
blocks.zh: A.10 滚动缓存窗口大小

blocks.en:
We ablate the number of past chunks n n retained in the rolling KV cache
(Sec. 3.5 ). Our default keeps a single past chunk ( n = 1 n=1 )
alongside the first-chunk anchor; here we compare it against a larger window that
also retains the second-to-last chunk ( n = 2 n=2 ). The n = 2 n=2 variant is a dedicated 4 4 -step student, whose Stage 2 is trained with the n = 2 n=2 attention mask; both are evaluated on Hallo3 test ( 10 10 s clips).
As reported in Table 11 ,
enlarging the window to n = 2 n=2 slightly improves FVD ( 193.2 193.2 vs. 195.5 195.5 ) at an equal FID, but degrades JEDi, identity, lip-sync and warping error, while increasing cache size and lowering throughput. This supports our minimal single-chunk cache as the best quality–efficiency trade-off.
